title: Episode 999: The Simpsons Spectacular Part I
summary: Episode 999 (Part I of a two-parter, billed as a milestone for the show's thousandth episode) is a deep dive into The Simpsons. The hosts cover the show's origins: the Tracy Ullman Show shorts starting in 1987, Matt Groening's Life in Hell comic and his pitch to James L. Brooks, and the December 1989 premiere that was Santa's Little Helper. They discuss how the show broke ground as a primetime animated series on Fox, its contrast with 1980s family sitcoms, and its rough early animation by Klasky Csupo and later Film Roman. They then cover the creative staff, the voice cast (Dan Castellaneta, Julie Kavner, Yeardley Smith, Nancy Cartwright, Hank Azaria, Harry Shearer, Pamela Hayden, Phil Hartman), memorable guest stars, and the show's referential humor. The episode ends with a cliffhanger as the hosts begin describing how an episode is made, including a table read they attended at the Fox lot. Part II is promised for the following Thursday.
topics: how The Simpsons episodes are made

segments.title: Episode 1000 milestone opening banter
segments.summary: The hosts mark the show's thousandth episode, explain that the Simpsons topic is split into a two-part episode, and share personal memories of first watching the show.

segments.title: Origins of The Simpsons and Tracy Ullman shorts
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Tracy Ullman Show shorts, the first episode 'Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire' and 'Santa's Little Helper', and how Matt Groening's Life in Hell comic led to the show after a pitch to James L. Brooks.
topics: Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire

segments.title: Simpsons as a revolution in family sitcoms and primetime animation
segments.summary: The hosts describe The Simpsons as the first primetime animated series since the early 1970s, its place on the new Fox network, and how it subverted the wholesome 1980s family sitcom alongside Married with Children and Roseanne.

segments.title: Early Bart era, animation studios, and early Homer voice
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Bart's early pop-culture fame and the T-shirt controversies, the early animation by Klasky Csupo and later Film Roman, the yellow skin choice, and how Homer's early voice differed.

segments.title: Writers and producers of the show
segments.summary: The hosts name key producers and writers, including Matt Groening, James L. Brooks, Sam Simon, Al Jean, and early writers George Meyer and John Schwartzwelder, and discuss the show's referential humor and Conan O'Brien's work on the show.

segments.title: Voice cast and recurring characters
segments.summary: The hosts walk through the main voice actors (Julie Kavner, Yeardley Smith, Dan Castellaneta, Nancy Cartwright, Harry Shearer, Pamela Hayden, Hank Azaria, Phil Hartman) and the many characters each performs, plus a brief note on the controversy around Apu.

segments.title: Memorable guest stars and musicians
segments.summary: The hosts list celebrity guest stars who played themselves or other characters, including Martin Sheen, Albert Brooks, Glenn Close, Johnny Cash, Kelsey Grammar, and musical guests, and mention the Critic crossover episode.

segments.title: How an episode is made and the table read
segments.summary: The hosts describe the writing process of an episode, including rewrites and the table read, and recount attending a table read at the Fox lot for an episode with Nick Offerman, meeting Matt Groening and cast members.

segments.title: Cliffhanger and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts tease Part II, promise it will air on Thursday, and share social media and website contact information.
